newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican teachers march again to back demands.
newsitem.headline: Mexican teachers march again to back demands.

text.p: At least 30,000 Mexican teachers from across the country marched in Mexico City on Wednesday in a second week of protests to seek better pay.

The teachers, part of the National Coordinating Council of Education Workers (CNTE), have been demonstrating several days a week in the capital since May 14, causing chaos in this traffic-choked city.
But they said they will keep snarling traffic as long as the government fails to agree to their demands.

In early May the government announced a salary rise of six percent for the teachers, plus an extra 10 percent in bonuses. The teachers called that ridiculous, saying their real salaries were dropping because of high inflation that hit 22 percent in the 12 months to April this year.
Teachers said their salaries ranged from 600 pesos ($75) to 1,400 pesos ($177) every two weeks, depending on which state employed them.
